facts.claim: Addis Ababa, meaning 'New Flower' in Amharic, was founded in 1886.

source.title: The New Flower: Addis Ababa and the Project of African Modernity
source.author: Amber N. Wiley
source.quote: Addis Ababa, or "New Flower" in Amharic, was founded in 1886.

facts.claim: Empress Taytu Betul, wife of Menelik II, is credited with selecting the site and with naming (renaming) the place.

source.title: Addis Ababa: Achilles' heel of Ethiopian Federation
source.author: Asrat Seyoum
source.quote: TaytuBetul, wife of Emperor Menelik II, is widely accredited for doing the initial sight selection.

facts.claim: The founding year varies between 1886 and 1888 depending on records; one account describes 1887 as the founding of a military garrison under Menilek II. The area was historically known as Finfinne, a name tied to its hot springs.

source.title: Establishment History of Addis Ababa and the Displacement of Oromo Communities from Finfinne
source.author: Chala Dandessa
source.tier: press (opinion/analysis; relays Oxford Research Encyclopedia of African History, not read directly)
source.quote: Addis Ababa is historically known as Finfinne, a name associated with the area's hot springs.

facts.claim: The OAU was created at a meeting in Addis Ababa in May 1963; its successor, the African Union, was launched in Durban in 2002.

places.name: Merkato
places.what: Merkato is an open-air market in western Addis Ababa, described in academic sources as the largest open market in Africa. Its present form dates to the Italian occupation, when it was named for the 'indigenous' population.

facts.label: Size claim
facts.value: Described as the largest open market in Africa

source.title: The Impact of Multi-Story Commercial Buildings on the Heritage Values of Market Open Market in Addis Ababa
source.publisher: OMICS Publishing Group, Journal of Architectural Engineering Technology 10(9)
source.author: Kibur Kassie and Daniel Lirebo
source.quote: It is still the largest open market in Africa.

facts.label: Italian name
facts.value: Italian occupiers called it 'Mercato indigenous', the market for natives

source.title: The Impact of Multi-Story Commercial Buildings on the Heritage Values of Market Open Market in Addis Ababa
source.publisher: OMICS Publishing Group, Journal of Architectural Engineering Technology 10(9)
source.author: Kibur Kassie and Daniel Lirebo
source.quote: The Italian occupiers called it Mercato indigenous which means in Italian the market for natives or indigenous market

facts.label: Italian-era relocation
facts.value: The existing market was moved to the north-western part of town

source.title: Menged Merkato
source.author: Emanuel Admassu
source.quote: Merkato indigeno—as named by the Italians—established its current location.

places.name: Adwa Victory Memorial
places.what: A memorial and museum complex in central Addis Ababa marking the Battle of Adwa, inaugurated in February 2024. It combines gates, statues and a museum.

places.name: Holy Trinity Cathedral
places.what: An Orthodox cathedral in Addis Ababa founded under Menelik II and completed in 1942. Its compound is a burial place for those who fought the Italian occupation.
